Advisory Committee On Homelessness (ACH) 11/10/2026 
 
Three-month Report (DRAFT) 
 
PURPOSE:  
 
The ACH was assigned to produce a report to the City approximately 
three months after its first convention and quarterly thereafter. 
Committee members were advised that any time during the 30-day 
window after 10/28 would be acceptable for submission of such a 
report. 
 
This report details the current progress of the ACH, its discoveries, 
connections it has made between city and community officials and 
expounds upon its planned mission trajectory.  
 
AREAS OF FOCUS:   
 
The ACH and its partners identified several areas of focus with acute relevance to the City and community 
members. These areas are designed specifically to make ACH’s preparations, progress and plans forefront and 
easily accessible. 
 
 (I.   Data Reviewed)    (II.   Feedback Reviewed)    (III.   Connections Established)  
(IV.   Subcommittees/Internal Structures Formed)    (V.   Mandate Compliance)    
(VI.   External Contributions)   (VII.   Strategy) 
 
 
I.   Data 
 
 Although the City specifically empaneled experts in homelessness, homelessness outreach, and public 
health into the ACH, ACH and its partners have been enduringly aware that in order to best serve our 
mandate we should review data from sources external to our domains of experience and re-review and 
seriously consider data as a standing priority to prepare for the delivery of as-needed recommendations as 
well as our final strategic plan. We reviewed the following data as part of our preparations and will 
continue to review data as it becomes available.  
 
● Documents reviewed: Robyn Stanicki memo dated 7/23/26
2/4 
II.   Feedback 
 
 ACH worked internally and with city officials to create a public comment session and establish official 
channels for ongoing feedback from constituents, unhoused community members, housed community 
members, affected others and subject matter experts. In addition, we have generally held ourselves to a 
standard of continually bringing forth feedback from our own domains of experience. We have not ruled 
out new public comment sessions and have mused about participating in, via subcommittee, or creating, 
standalone listening sessions; Given time constraints and appointment limits we are considering the public 
comment period partially complete as to truly give strategic planning prioritization.  
 
● ACH successfully created and attended a public comment session on 8/11/26 
● ACH established official channels (city email) and accountability structure (standing agenda 
priorities) for reviewing new and ongoing community feedback.  
 
III.   Connections 
 
 Before strategizing can begin or be undertaken enduringly, ACH has acknowledged that our logical first 
step should be creating a group environment and work format that is serviceable and well-informed for all 
of us. To do that, we have focused these first three months on acclimatization to each other as co-workers 
and relationship and knowledge building of other Bangor- area and City experts in the homelessness crisis.   
 
 
IV.   Internality 
 
 ACH has formed internal subcommittees and workflows to increase overall committee efficiency and 
productivity. We also successfully complied with our charter and workflow needs by appointing a chair 
person, Alton Buzzell (committee member and Marketing Director, Hollywood Casino), and a secretary, 
Ben Treat (committee member and Executive Director, Bangor Public Library).  
 
● Warming Shelter Subcommittee formed. 
 
 
V.   Mandate Compliance
3/4 
 ACH has been advised on and worked faithfully on several matters concerning our mandate to deliver a 
12-month, data-driven, strategic plan to improve the matter of homelessness within the City. We have also 
already delivered work product on the aspect of our mandate that concerns providing as-needed and 
improvisational recommendations to the City and our partners. Additionally, we received education from 
legal and ethical professionals within the City on ethical committee conduct. All members have made and 
transparently discussed appropriate recusals and accountability measures concerning their own areas (if 
present) of conflict. Importantly, within our first few months, in addition to creating a serviceable work 
environment, we have constructed and semi-finalized a system to deliver our strategic plan (see  VII. 
Strategy). 
 
● Convened 8 meetings of the Committee. 
● Created workflow for overall strategic plan. 
● Consulted on Yellen Pines, Project HOPE, Day Center, and Warming Shelter. 
 
VI.  Externality 
 
 ACH is aware that the crisis of homelessness is not new and that Bangor experts, community members, 
and people within and without our ecosystem have long worked on this as a public health topic and 
community issue. Within the Bangor area, there are many non-profits, politicians, faith leaders, 
community advocates and constituents that have already produced meaningful work product, 
improvements, and guidelines pertinent to this subject. We have specifically reviewed those items as a 
committee and in our individual capacities to ensure we are not creating duplicate work, assessing our 
own areas of bias and making sure that Bangorian voices are heard and respected.  
 
● Councilor Carolyn Fish Plan  
● The Bangor Opportunity Plan 
● Jonathan Sprague Plan 
● Other emails and feedback 
 
VII.  Strategy 
 
 We have agreed on and thoroughly discussed a format to deliver our 12-month strategic plan, which is our 
foremost committee priority. Our plan is to create recommendations, focusing on policies and elements 
within the City’s direct influence, using a recursive methodology. ACH acknowledges that this plan is not 
all-inclusive, nor is it designed to be; This plan is part of our overall triage strategy to address the areas of 
critical concern within our mandate. When we release this strategy,  it will be with the contingency that it 
is a living document intended to be modified, expounded upon and resculpted to fit whatever current 
needs the future City or its partners have.  The areas of strategic concern for the purposes of this plan are
4/4 
detailed here. We have been careful to discuss inclusion of design philosophies that are at least partially 
representative of the committee’s various expertise, our community’s experiences, and overall knowledge 
and data from the Bangor area; Though we intend none of those philosophies to be the final word in our 
strategizing, we acknowledge that not including them would likely not create a sufficiently tailored 
strategy for the City.  
 
● Prevent: Reduce new cases of homelessness 
● Connect: Broker services that reduce homelessness or its risk to relevant community members 
● Shelter: Directly provision services and sheltering to homeless or at-risk individuals 
● Stabilize: Create and audit current accessible entry into the homelessness services ecosystem to increase 
overall likelihood in becoming housed 
● House: Work with housing, real estate, and public sectors to make sure that homelessness has a viable, 
safe, and durable endpoint 
● Retain: Ensure current strategies and resources last. Make perennial reduction in homelessness and its 
morbidities.  Keep people from falling outside of the scope of the ecosystem unnecessarily 
 
☆.  Word from the committee 
 
During our discussion of the three-month report it came up that it would be preferential to receive, as a 
product of this report, feedback from the council and our community itself. We hope that our provision of this 
report can give us advanced notice as to the direct areas of success, concern, and suggestion from the 
stakeholders before we start encoding increasingly fixed points into the strategic plan.

City of Bangor Prevention Activities 
Public Health and Community Services Department 
Housing Navigation & Stabilization 
The Eviction & Stabilization Navigator works directly with tenants and property owners to identify 
solutions that can prevent eviction and keep residents safely housed. Referrals come from landlords, 
individuals, community-based organizations, social services agencies and other entities. This 
originated with MaineHousing funding that supported a position and funds to help with eviction 
prevention expenses. 
Assistance that supports prevention: 
- Addressing rental financial challenges 
- Resolving cleanliness and housekeeping concerns 
- Supporting tenants experiencing behavioral or lease compliance issues 
-, Improving communication between tenants and landlords 
By working collaboratively with all parties involved, the Navigator helps develop practical solutions 
that prevent individuals and families from losing their housing and entering homelessness. 
 
Homeless Response Coordinator 
The Homeless Response Coordinator works closely with community partners to identify housing 
solutions and prevent homelessness before it occurs with the following  
• Hospital case managers 
• Jail and correctional facility case managers 
• Social service agencies 
• Housing providers 
• Community organizations 
• Landlords 
Through coordination and problem solving, the City helps individual’s access resources and develop 
housing plans that support long-term stability and not be left to live on the streets.
General Assistance 
General Assistance is an important homelessness prevention resource for eligible Bangor residents. 
When an individual or family qualifies, this program may provide financial support that helps address 
immediate needs and maintain housing during times of crisis and prevents them becoming homeless 
 
Rental Assistance Program (Permanent Supportive 
Housing) 
Rental Assistance Program continues to support individuals housed through Permanent Supportive 
Housing vouchers. Landlords, clients, case managers will contact when housing issues arise to 
problem solve in order to prevent evictions.  
 
Suggestions for prevention  
- Landlord liaison program - person able to be that liaison between tenants and landlords 
  
- Retention Navigators – navigators working with a certain group with lots of Barriers to help 
support them while in housing  
 
- Programs to help with the gap of evenings and weekends when most issues arise
